questions.question: How does the psalmist describe his attitude in Psalm 131?
options: His heart is not lifted up; he has calmed and quieted his soul
His mouth is never once silent; he sings aloud the LORD's praise
His eyes are not ever closed; he watches and waits for the morning
His hands are never once idle; he labors hard from dawn to dusk
questions.answer: His heart is not lifted up; he has calmed and quieted his soul

questions.question: To what does the psalmist compare his quieted soul?
options: A traveler asleep in the shade
A bird at rest in its nest
A weaned child with its mother
A young lamb beside the shepherd
questions.answer: A weaned child with its mother

questions.question: The psalm ends urging Israel to hope in the LORD from this time forth and forevermore.
O LORD, my heart is not proud; my eyes are not _____.
I have calmed and quieted my soul, like a weaned child with its _____.
